root.name: Van Geet Opening: Jendrossek Gambit
root.moves: 1. Nc3 d5 2. f4 d4 3. Ne4 f5 4. Nf2 Nf6 5. Nf3 c5 6. b4

overview: A Van Geet reply to 1...d5 with f4, where after 2...d4 3.Ne4 f5 4.Nf2 White has retreated the knight and Black has space. 6.b4 offers a pawn to open the queenside, and ...cxb4 leaves White behind in material with some development. Rare and speculative; the details are not well known to me.

white_ideas.idea: Offer b4 to open lines against Black's queenside and gain tempo on c5
Bring pieces out quickly and use the e5/d4 squares

black_ideas.idea: Take on b4 and keep the extra pawn
Hold the space gained with the d4 and f5 pawns

typical_structures.structure: Black pawns on d4, f5 and c5 against White's f4; the centre is semi-closed

character.notes: A pawn is offered with White already behind in space; unbalanced.

gambit.notes: 6.b4 cxb4 keeps the pawn for Black.

soundness.notes: White has lost time with the knight and the pawn offer looks hard to justify.

structure.notes: d4/f5/c5 centre fixed, semi-open b-file after ...cxb4.

approach.notes: A rare gambit within an irregular opening.

level.notes: Dubious and obscure, not a good first repertoire choice.

character.reason: A gambit in a locked-up centre leads to unbalanced play.

gambit.reason: 6.b4 is a pawn Black can take and keep.

soundness.reason: White is behind in space and the pawn offer lacks sound support.

structure.reason: Centre fixed on d4 but the queenside is still open to change.

approach.reason: Rare gambit of an already irregular opening.

level.reason: Dubious so not Beginner; little to learn.
